conviction_note: A routine quarter for a low-volatility property company that updates a mechanical 'current portfolio + announced acquisitions' forecast every quarter (raised at each of the last five reports). The one new fact, nine acquisitions for MSEK 341 announced 15:00 CEST on 14 Oct, was in the 14 Oct close (+1.3% on about twice normal volume). Small positives (likely forecast nudge, flat Riksbank rate through Q3) roughly cancel small negatives (per-ordinary-share dilution from the June preference issue, the sector sell-off on long rates, a board member's sale on 31 Aug). So the findings sum to +0.1 and p_up sits at 53 on abs_move 3.5, giving +0.21.

findings.finding: Emilshus announced nine light-industrial acquisitions for MSEK 341 (rental value MSEK 31) the afternoon before the print, with most closings in Q4. Its forecast covers 'current property portfolio and announced acquisitions' and has been raised at every report, so the Q3 release will very likely lift the FY2026 PFPM forecast from MSEK 495 to roughly 498-505.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forecast was raised at each recent report: Q3 2025 (+10 to 410), FY2025 (first 2026 guide 480), Q1 2026 (490), Q2 2026 (495). Observed report-day moves: 2025-10-15 +2.0%, 2026-02-06 -0.55%, 2026-04-21 -3.11%, 2026-07-10 +1.11%. Raises were not rewarded consistently.
findings.why_not_priced: The acquisition itself was in the 14 Oct close: +1.29% on 33,954 shares against a 20-day norm of roughly 15-20k. What the price cannot yet hold is the forecast number, because the company has not stated how much these deals add to 2026. Danske's model explicitly excludes unannounced deals. If the raise were fully priced, the 14 Oct move would have been larger than a normal day's 1.3% sigma.
findings.independence: Danske's initiation says its forecasts exclude non-announced acquisitions, which implies upside to estimates: https://www.placera.se/telegram/emilshus-diversifiering-minskar-risk-kop-danske-20261006

findings.finding: The Riksbank held its policy rate at 1.75% through Q3 (August and September decisions), so Emilshus's floating funding cost was flat in the quarter. Together with Q3's seasonally low operating costs and the MSEK 614 deal closed in July, that points to Q3 PFPM near or slightly above Danske's +19% (about MSEK 134).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 PFPM +48% y/y came with a +2.0% report-day move; Q1 2026 per-share +11% came with -3.1%.
findings.original_quote: Penningpolitiskt beslut september 2026 – styrräntan lämnas oförändrad på 1,75 procent (rate left unchanged at 1.75%)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside the company's own guided H2 of about MSEK 254. It is filed because it removes a downside path (a funding-cost surprise), not because the market lacks it.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 report shows Q3 is the seasonal high (Q2 98 -> Q3 113 -> Q4 110): https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b04640eab2a75d3bd5844b28febd2d32c&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: The June 2026 issue of 12 million preference shares (SEK 2.00 a year each) raised the preference claim on PFPM by about MSEK 6 a quarter. Q3 PFPM per ordinary share is therefore likely up only about 14% y/y (about SEK 0.89 against 0.78) while headline PFPM is up about 19%, i.e. under the company's 15%-per-year per-share target for the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 per-ordinary-share growth of +11% (below target), against a +26% headline, came with a -3.11% report-day move. That is the only prior quarter where per-share growth fell below 15%.
findings.why_not_priced: The issue is public, but Danske's published figure and the press headline are total PFPM (+19%), not per ordinary share. The per-share gap is my arithmetic from the issuer's share counts, not a number anyone has printed. If it were priced, the per-share target would already have come up in the Danske/Direkt coverage, which it does not.

findings.finding: Swedish listed property has sold off on rising long rates since early September (Catena 384.8 -> 333.6, -13%; Emilshus 51.6 -> 43.3, -16%). Emilshus's own preference share drifted from SEK 30.4 to 28.3, a higher yield on its marginal equity. That raises the risk of a flat or negative Q3 valuation line and a NAV that does not grow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Emilshus has reported positive property value changes every quarter since 2024 (Q2 2026 +64 MSEK, Q1 +32), so a negative print on this line would be new.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the 16% drawdown in the B share is the market already marking this. It is filed because the release turns the macro into a reported value change and NAV. It is macro-to-company transmission, a hypothesis until the report states the valuation yield.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.33) is a mild contrarian read of the -6.7% 20-day run-up; the findings roughly net to zero, so they neither confirm nor fight it.
language_note: The FI insider register (Swedish only) carried the board member's 31 Aug sale of 300,000 B shares at SEK 51. English searches surfaced it only as an unsourced tracker line.
Nyhetsbyrån Direkt (placera.se / efn.se, Swedish) carried Danske's initiation and its Q3 bar (+24% rental income, +19% PFPM), which no English source returned.
The issuer's own releases are bilingual and the English versions carried everything the Swedish ones did.
lessons_applied: 'Too small about the move' and 'the move is in the guide': abs_move_pct raised from 3.0 to 3.5, since a forecast change is likely. Kept well under the 9% guidance median because the change is mechanical, small and expected, and the name's observed report-day moves were 0.6-3.1%.
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': sector/rates finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
'Proxy / already public': board-member sale cut from -0.2 to -0.1; preference-dilution inference cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because the issue is public.
